<section class="level2 unnumbered safe-appendix-heading" id="sec-model-equations">
<h2 class="unnumbered safe-appendix-heading anchored" data-anchor-id="sec-model-equations"><span class="safe-appendix-label"><strong>Appendix F</strong></span><br/>
<span class="safe-appendix-title"><strong>Model Equations</strong></span></h2>
<p><strong>Scope.</strong> This appendix carries forward the structure and model components of the 2024 <em>Appendix EBS Pollock Model Description</em> (SAFE pp. 172–182). The equations describe the Model 23.0 ADMB comparison. The proposed Model 26.0 configuration and its weight schedules are described in <a class="quarto-xref" href="#sec-approach">Section 5</a> and <a class="quarto-xref" href="#sec-fishery-weights">Section 4.1.3</a>. The historical Tier 1 material documents an available calculation; the December 2024 SSC adopted Tier 3a.</p>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="dynamics">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="dynamics">Dynamics</h3>
<p>The statistical age-structured model combines the catch equation with annual survival and an accumulating terminal age group <span class="citation" data-cites="Fournier1982 hilborn1992 schnute1995 mcallister1997">(<a href="#ref-Fournier1982" role="doc-biblioref">Fournier and Archibald 1982</a>; <a href="#ref-hilborn1992" role="doc-biblioref">Hilborn and Walters 1992</a>; <a href="#ref-schnute1995" role="doc-biblioref">Schnute and Richards 1995</a>; <a href="#ref-mcallister1997" role="doc-biblioref">McAllister and Ianelli 1997</a>)</span>. Let <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> index years, <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a=1,\ldots,A</annotation></semantics></math> index ages, and <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A=15</annotation></semantics></math> denote ages 15 and older. <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{t,a}</annotation></semantics></math> is abundance at the start of the year, <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{t,a}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{t,a}</annotation></semantics></math> are annual instantaneous mortality rates, and <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{t,a}</annotation></semantics></math> is their sum. Catch at age and catch biomass are</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-catch"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mfrac><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub></mfrac><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>−</mi><msub><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msup><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>A</mi></munderover><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mi>f</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mi>f</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>b</mi></munder><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mi>.</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\begin{aligned}
Z_{t,a}&amp;=F_{t,a}+M_{t,a},\\
C_{t,a}&amp;=N_{t,a}\frac{F_{t,a}}{Z_{t,a}}(1-e^{-Z_{t,a}}),\\
Y_t&amp;=\sum_{a=1}^{A}C_{t,a}w^{f}_{t,a},\qquad
p^f_{t,a}=\frac{C_{t,a}}{\sum_b C_{t,b}}.
\end{aligned}
 \qquad(2)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>Here <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mi>f</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w^f_{t,a}</annotation></semantics></math> is fishery weight-at-age. Abundance in millions of fish multiplied by kg per fish gives biomass in kt. The population advances as</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-survival"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>−</mi><msub><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></mtd><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>−</mi><msub><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>−</mi><msub><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msup><mi>.</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\begin{aligned}
N_{t+1,1}&amp;=R_{t+1},\\
N_{t+1,a+1}&amp;=N_{t,a}e^{-Z_{t,a}}, &amp;&amp;1\leq a&lt;A,\\
N_{t+1,A}&amp;=N_{t,A-1}e^{-Z_{t,A-1}}+N_{t,A}e^{-Z_{t,A}}.
\end{aligned}
 \qquad(3)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>The middle line applies to entry from each younger age; the final line adds surviving members of the plus group. This corrects the age subscript in 2024 Eq. 14.2, which printed <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a-1</annotation></semantics></math> on the right side while advancing <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> to <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a+1</annotation></semantics></math> on the left.</p>
<p>Fishing mortality separates annual intensity from selectivity at age:</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-fishing-selectivity"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mi>f</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>F</mi></msub><msup><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></msup><mi>.</mi><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
F_{t,a}=s^f_{t,a}\mu_F e^{\epsilon_t}.
 \qquad(4)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>The assessment estimates selectivity coefficients with penalties on changes over time and on curvature across ages <span class="citation" data-cites="butterworth2003ajms">(<a href="#ref-butterworth2003ajms" role="doc-biblioref">Butterworth et al. 2003</a>)</span>. In a general penalty notation, <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_t\log s_{t,a}</annotation></semantics></math> controls annual changes and <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_a^2\log s_{t,a}</annotation></semantics></math> controls smoothness across ages. Their weights and allowed change years come from the run controls.</p>
<p>The bottom-trawl survey (BTS) uses logistic selectivity above age one and a separate age-one term. The implemented form is</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-bts-selectivity"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mi>b</mi></msubsup></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>−</mi><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>50</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">]</mo><msup><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">}</mo><mrow><mi>−</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></mtd><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mi>a</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>b</mi></msubsup></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><mover><mi>k</mi><mo accent="true">‾</mo></mover><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>50</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mover><mi>a</mi><mo accent="true">‾</mo></mover><mn>50</mn></msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>.</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\begin{aligned}
s^{b}_{t,a}&amp;=\{1+\exp[-k_t(a-a_{50,t})]\}^{-1}, &amp;&amp;a&gt;1,\\
\log s^{b}_{t,1}&amp;=b_1\exp(d_t),\\
k_t&amp;=\bar k\exp(u_t),\qquad a_{50,t}=\bar a_{50}\exp(v_t).
\end{aligned}
 \qquad(5)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>This follows <code>compute_selectivity()</code> and the age-one assignment in <code>Get_Selectivity()</code>. It replaces the ambiguous slope/intercept and age-one expressions printed in 2024. The 2024 description reported a process variance of 0.04 for an earlier random-walk formulation. The retained controls instead select the penalty on changes in log-selectivity at the specified ages, plus the separate age-one deviation penalty. Its coefficient is 8 for the squared first differences of <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_t</annotation></semantics></math>. The actual controls and source identify which parameter or log-selectivity penalty is applied.</p>
<p>Acoustic-trawl survey (ATS) selectivity is flexible across ages; the optional separate age-one index leaves ages 2–15+ in its composition likelihood. Constant survey catchability and time-varying selectivity represent separate model components.</p>
</section>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="recruitment">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="recruitment">Recruitment</h3>
<p>Recruitment is abundance at age one. Female spawning biomass accounts for survival from the start of the year to spawning:</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-spawning-biomass"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>A</mi></munderover><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>−</mi><mi>τ</mi><msub><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mi>s</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.25</mn><mi>.</mi><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
B_t=\sum_{a=1}^{A}N_{t,a}\exp(-\tau Z_{t,a})\phi_a w^s_{t,a},
\qquad \tau=0.25.
 \qquad(6)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>Here <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mi>s</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w^s_{t,a}</annotation></semantics></math> is spawning weight and <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_a</annotation></semantics></math> includes both maturity and the female fraction. The assessment reads a maturity schedule and applies the female fraction internally; the one-sex SPM handoff reads maturity and halves total abundance. Applying the female fraction once preserves the same biomass definition. The spawning time is April 1 (month 4).</p>
<p>Annual recruitment deviations accompany a stock–recruit function, <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_t=f(B_{t-1})\exp(\varepsilon_t)</annotation></semantics></math>, with log-scale deviation penalties and the implementation’s bias adjustment. The Ricker option selected by <code>SrType=1</code> is</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-ricker"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>B</mi><msub><mi>ψ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mspace width="-0.167em"></mspace><mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="true">[</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="true">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>B</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mfrac><mo form="postfix" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo form="postfix" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><msub><mi>ψ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mspace width="-0.167em"></mspace><mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo form="postfix" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>.</mi><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
f(B)=\frac{B}{\psi_0}\exp\!\left[\alpha_R\left(1-\frac{B}{B_0}\right)\right],
\qquad B_0=R_0\psi_0,\qquad
\alpha_R=\log\!\left(\frac{4h_{\mathrm{ADMB}}}{1-h_{\mathrm{ADMB}}}\right).
 \qquad(7)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p><math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>ψ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi_0</annotation></semantics></math> is unfished spawning biomass per recruit. The final expression is the source code’s transformation of its parameter named steepness; it is retained as <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{\mathrm{ADMB}}</annotation></semantics></math> to identify that convention. The 2024 printed Ricker equation misplaced <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_0</annotation></semantics></math> in the biomass ratio. The expression here follows <code>SRecruit()</code> and <code>Get_Bzero()</code> in the preserved template.</p>
<p>The alternative Beverton–Holt relationship <span class="citation" data-cites="francis1992use">(<a href="#ref-francis1992use" role="doc-biblioref">Francis 1992</a>)</span> is</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-beverton-holt"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow></msub><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>B</mi><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow></msub><mi>B</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>ψ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>h</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msub><mi>β</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>h</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>h</mi><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac><mi>.</mi><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
f_{\mathrm{BH}}(B)=\frac{B}{\alpha_{\mathrm{BH}}+\beta_{\mathrm{BH}}B},\qquad
\alpha_{\mathrm{BH}}=\psi_0\frac{1-h}{4h},\qquad
\beta_{\mathrm{BH}}=\frac{5h-1}{4hR_0}.
 \qquad(8)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>For this alternative, <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is the fraction of unfished recruitment at 20% of unfished spawning biomass. The 2024 controls fix <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_R=1</annotation></semantics></math> and specify a symmetric beta prior with shape parameters 14.93209877 for the selected stock–recruit parameter. The earlier Beverton–Holt example in the 2024 appendix used a different prior; it remains an alternative rather than the selected 2024 setting.</p>
</section>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="diagnostics">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="diagnostics">Diagnostics</h3>
<p>The historical replay diagnostic retains fitted recruitment anomalies while adjusting recruitment for the change in spawning biomass under a hypothetical history with fishing set to zero:</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-replay"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mover><mi>R</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mi>.</mi><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
R'_t=\widehat R_t\frac{f(B'_{t-1})}{f(B_{t-1})}.
 \qquad(9)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>Retrospective analyses repeat estimation after removing recent years and compare estimates for common years <span class="citation" data-cites="parma1993 ianelli1998">(<a href="#ref-parma1993" role="doc-biblioref">Parma 1993</a>; <a href="#ref-ianelli1998" role="doc-biblioref">Ianelli and Fournier 1998</a>)</span>. Their fit controls and terminal years accompany each saved run.</p>
<p>The effective number of ages contributing to spawning biomass is the exponential of Shannon entropy <span class="citation" data-cites="jost2006">(<a href="#ref-jost2006" role="doc-biblioref">Jost 2006</a>)</span>:</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-age-diversity"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mspace width="-0.167em"></mspace><mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="true">(</mo><mi>−</mi><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>a</mi></munder><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mo form="postfix" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>−</mi><mi>τ</mi><msub><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msup><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mi>s</mi></msubsup></mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mfrac><mi>.</mi><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
D_t=\exp\!\left(-\sum_a p^{B}_{t,a}\log p^{B}_{t,a}\right),\qquad
p^{B}_{t,a}=\frac{N_{t,a}e^{-\tau Z_{t,a}}\phi_a w^s_{t,a}}{B_t}.
 \qquad(10)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>The mean-age diagnostic uses observed and predicted composition means and the predicted variance at age <span class="citation" data-cites="francis2011weighting">(<a href="#ref-francis2011weighting" role="doc-biblioref">Francis 2011</a>)</span>:</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-mean-age"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mover><mi>a</mi><mo accent="true">‾</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>a</mi></munder><mi>a</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msub><mover><mover><mi>a</mi><mo accent="true">‾</mo></mover><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>a</mi></munder><mi>a</mi><msub><mover><mi>p</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>a</mi></munder><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mover><mover><mi>a</mi><mo accent="true">‾</mo></mover><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><msup><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><msub><mover><mi>p</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mover><mi>a</mi><mo accent="true">‾</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover><mover><mi>a</mi><mo accent="true">‾</mo></mover><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mi>/</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msqrt></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mi>ν</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mi>t</mi></msub><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">}</mo><mrow><mi>−</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>.</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>11</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\begin{aligned}
\bar a_t&amp;=\sum_a a p_{t,a},\qquad
\widehat{\bar a}_t=\sum_a a\widehat p_{t,a},\\
V_t&amp;=\sum_a(a-\widehat{\bar a}_t)^2\widehat p_{t,a},\\
z_t&amp;=\frac{\bar a_t-\widehat{\bar a}_t}{\sqrt{V_t/n_t}},\qquad
\nu=\{\operatorname{Var}_t(z_t)\}^{-1}.
\end{aligned}
 \qquad(11)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>The implied adjusted sample size is <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>ν</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu n_t</annotation></semantics></math>. This diagnostic supports evaluation of weighting; changing assessment inputs requires a decision. The expression for <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_t</annotation></semantics></math> replaces the malformed <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>κ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_t</annotation></semantics></math> formula in the printed 2024 appendix.</p>
</section>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="parameter-estimation">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="parameter-estimation">Parameter estimation</h3>
<p>The objective adds negative log likelihoods, prior densities and selectivity penalties. Phase-based estimation introduces parameters in stages. For age compositions, the multinomial contribution, up to a data-only constant, is</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-age-likelihood"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>−</mi><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>t</mi></munder><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>a</mi></munder><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover><mi>p</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msubsup><mover><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">𝒑</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mspace width="0.167em"></mspace><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mover><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">𝒑</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mspace width="0.167em"></mspace><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow></mrow></msubsup><mi>E</mi><mi>.</mi><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\ell_{\mathrm{age}}=-\sum_t n_t\sum_a p_{t,a}\log(\widehat p_{t,a}+c),
\qquad \widehat{\boldsymbol p}^{\,\mathrm{read}}_t
=\widehat{\boldsymbol p}^{\,\mathrm{true}}_t E.
 \qquad(12)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p><math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> is the small numerical constant in the implementation. When enabled, <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{a,b}</annotation></semantics></math> is the probability that true age <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> is read as age <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>. The selected historical controls have <code>use_age_err=0</code>. The original appendix also described a robust composition option <span class="citation" data-cites="fournier1990multifan">(<a href="#ref-fournier1990multifan" role="doc-biblioref">Fournier et al. 1990</a>)</span>, with variance inflation and a small outlier component. In the retained 2024 controls its activation phase is 1350; the six-phase completed comparison uses the multinomial form. This distinction prevents the general software description from implying that the robust option was active.</p>
<p>For survey <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> at within-year time <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_s</annotation></semantics></math>, expected abundance and biomass at age are</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-survey-predictions"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover><mi>N</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mi>s</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mi>s</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>−</mi><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><msub><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msubsup><mover><mi>I</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mi>s</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>a</mi></munder><msubsup><mover><mi>N</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mi>s</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mi>s</mi></msubsup><mi>.</mi><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>13</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\widehat N^s_{t,a}=q_s s^s_{t,a}N_{t,a}e^{-\tau_s Z_{t,a}},\qquad
\widehat I^s_t=\sum_a\widehat N^s_{t,a}w^s_{t,a}.
 \qquad(13)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>An abundance index omits the weight multiplier. The original description used midyear survey timing; actual run inputs specify the timing used in each comparison. The AVO index shares ATS selectivity and its documented weight basis, while retaining a separate catchability coefficient.</p>
<p>The independent lognormal-index and multivariate BTS contributions have the forms</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-index-likelihood"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>t</mi></munder><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><msubsup><mi>I</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><msub><mover><mi>I</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">]</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">𝒓</mi><mi mathvariant="sans-serif">𝖳</mi></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mi>−</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">𝒓</mi><mo>,</mo><mspace width="1.0em"></mspace><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><msubsup><mi>I</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><msub><mover><mi>I</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mi>.</mi><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>14</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\ell_s=\frac12\sum_t\frac{[\log I^{\mathrm{obs}}_{s,t}-\log\widehat I_{s,t}]^2}
{\sigma^2_{s,t}},\qquad
\ell_{\mathrm{BTS}}=\frac12\boldsymbol r^{\mathsf{T}}\Sigma^{-1}\boldsymbol r,
\quad r_t=\log I^{\mathrm{obs}}_t-\log\widehat I_t.
 \qquad(14)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>Fixed-variance normalization terms are constant for these comparisons. The normal-index option described in 2024 instead uses residuals on the original scale. The BTS covariance provides <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> for the multivariate lognormal fit. Catch biomass enters the implemented objective as <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>t</mi></msub><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover><mi>Y</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">]</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_C\sum_t[\log(Y_t^{\mathrm{obs}}+c)-\log(\widehat Y_t+c)]^2</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_C=200</annotation></semantics></math> in the retained controls. This equals <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/(2\sigma_C^2)</annotation></semantics></math> for <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_C=0.05</annotation></semantics></math> and removes the extra factor of two in the printed 2024 likelihood expression. Priors and penalties retain their actual source-code weights.</p>
</section>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="uncertainty-in-mean-body-mass">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="uncertainty-in-mean-body-mass">Uncertainty in mean body mass</h3>
<p>The 2024 appendix described estimating future weights within the assessment to propagate uncertainty into derived quantities <span class="citation" data-cites="ianelli2001">(<a href="#ref-ianelli2001" role="doc-biblioref">Ianelli and Williamson 2001</a>)</span>. Its earlier option used <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>∼</mo><mi mathvariant="script">𝒩</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover><mi>w</mi><mo accent="true">‾</mo></mover><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w^{\mathrm{future}}_a\sim\mathcal{N}(\bar w_a,\sigma_{w,a}^2)</annotation></semantics></math>. The retained implementation fits a mean growth curve plus cohort and year effects. For starting modeled age <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_0</annotation></semantics></math>, its mean curve is</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-mean-weight"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover><mi>w</mi><mo accent="true">‾</mo></mover><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>w</mi></msub><msup><mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="true">{</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo form="postfix" stretchy="true">}</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>.</mi><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>15</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\bar w_a=\alpha_w\left\{L_1+(L_2-L_1)
\frac{1-K^{a-a_0}}{1-K^{A-1}}\right\}^{3}.
 \qquad(15)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>At the final estimation phase, the recurrence in <code>Est_Fixed_Effects_wts()</code> is</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-weight-effects"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mover><mi>w</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><msub><mover><mi>w</mi><mo accent="true">‾</mo></mover><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mover><mi>w</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><msub><mover><mi>w</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover><mi>w</mi><mo accent="true">‾</mo></mover><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover><mi>w</mi><mo accent="true">‾</mo></mover><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>y</mi></msub><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo></mtd><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mi>a</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mi>.</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>16</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\begin{aligned}
\widehat w_{t,a_0}&amp;=\bar w_{a_0}
\exp(\sigma_c^2/2+\sigma_c c_t),\\
\widehat w_{t,a}&amp;=\widehat w_{t-1,a-1}
+(\bar w_a-\bar w_{a-1})\exp(\sigma_y^2/2+\sigma_y y_t), &amp;&amp;a&gt;a_0.
\end{aligned}
 \qquad(16)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>The initial year starts at <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mover><mi>w</mi><mo accent="true">‾</mo></mover><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar w_a</annotation></semantics></math>; dataset-specific scale vectors map the latent weights to observation series. This notation corrects the increment index in 2024 and explicitly retains the implementation’s sigma scaling and final-phase offsets. The cohort and year deviations receive standard-normal penalties. The four-term weight objective is</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-weight-likelihood"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mi>w</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><munder><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msub><mover><mi>w</mi><mo accent="true">‾</mo></mover><mi>a</mi></msub><msup><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><munder><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msub><mover><mi>w</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>t</mi></munder><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>t</mi></munder><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mi>.</mi><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>17</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\ell_w=\frac12\sum_{h,t,a}
\frac{(w^{\mathrm{obs}}_{h,t,a}-\bar w_a)^2}{\sigma^2_{h,t,a}}
+\frac12\sum_{h,t,a}
\frac{(w^{\mathrm{obs}}_{h,t,a}-\widehat w_{h,t,a})^2}{\sigma^2_{h,t,a}}
+\frac12\sum_t c_t^2+\frac12\sum_t y_t^2.
 \qquad(17)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>The 2026 numerical baseline allocates all four terms and retains their sum.</p>
</section>

<p>The 2024 description retained a Tier 1 calculation based on fishable biomass, the harmonic-mean harvest rate at MSY, and a spawning-biomass adjustment:</p>

padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><msubsup><mover><mi>B</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mi>f</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mi>f</mi></msup></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">}</mo><mo>,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mover><mi>u</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></mrow></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-right: 0"><msub><mi>ζ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="true">{</mo><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left"><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mi>/</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>0.05</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>/</mi><mn>0.95</mn><mo>,</mo></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left"><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left"><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left"><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></mrow></msub><mi>.</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>18</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\begin{aligned}
ABC_t&amp;=B^f_{{\mathrm{GM}},t}\widehat u_{\mathrm{HM}}\zeta_t,\\
B^f_{{\mathrm{GM}},t}&amp;=\exp\{\log\widehat B^f_t-\sigma^2_{\log B^f}/2\},\\
\widehat u_{\mathrm{HM}}&amp;=\exp\{\log\widehat u_{\mathrm{MSY}}-\sigma^2_{\log u}/2\},\\
\zeta_t&amp;=\begin{cases}
(B_t/B_{\mathrm{MSY}}-0.05)/0.95,&amp;B_t&lt;B_{\mathrm{MSY}},\\
1,&amp;B_t\geq B_{\mathrm{MSY}}.
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
 \qquad(18)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>The geometric and harmonic adjustments assume the documented lognormal approximations. This historical formula describes the earlier calculation over its applicable biomass range; final advice uses the adopted tier and the complete corresponding harvest-control rule.</p>
</section>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="tier-3-projections">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="tier-3-projections">Tier 3 projections</h3>
<p>For fixed mortality, maturity, weights and selectivity, equilibrium spawning biomass per recruit at fishing intensity <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> is</p>
<p><span id="eq-admb-tier3-spr"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>F</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msub><mi>l</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>F</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>l</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>F</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>−</mi><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>F</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></mtd><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mn>1</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mi>l</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>F</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>l</mi><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>F</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>−</mi><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>F</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>−</mi><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>F</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><mi>ψ</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>F</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>a</mi></munder><msub><mi>l</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>F</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi></msubsup><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>−</mi><mi>τ</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>F</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right" style="text-align: right; padding-right: 0"><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>100</mn><mi>%</mi></mrow></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="left" style="text-align: left; padding-left: 0"><mo>=</mo><mover><mi>R</mi><mo accent="true">‾</mo></mover><mi>ψ</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mi>%</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>100</mn></mfrac><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>100</mn><mi>%</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mfrac><mrow><mi>ψ</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mi>%</mi></mrow></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>ψ</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>100</mn></mfrac><mi>.</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>19</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\begin{aligned}
l_1(F)&amp;=1,\qquad l_a(F)=l_{a-1}(F)e^{-M_{a-1}-Fs_{a-1}}, &amp;&amp;1&lt;a&lt;A,\\
l_A(F)&amp;=\frac{l_{A-1}(F)e^{-M_{A-1}-Fs_{A-1}}}{1-e^{-M_A-Fs_A}},\\
\psi(F)&amp;=\sum_a l_a(F)\phi_a w^s_a e^{-\tau(M_a+Fs_a)},\\
B_{100\%}&amp;=\bar R\psi(0),\qquad
B_{x\%}=\frac{x}{100}B_{100\%},\qquad
\frac{\psi(F_{x\%})}{\psi(0)}=\frac{x}{100}.
\end{aligned}
 \qquad(19)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>Tier 3a uses <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>40</mn><mi>%</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{40\%}</annotation></semantics></math> for maximum ABC and <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>35</mn><mi>%</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{35\%}</annotation></semantics></math> for OFL, with the adopted biomass-dependent rule applied when needed. Projection catch follows <a class="quarto-xref" href="#eq-admb-catch">Equation 2</a>. The 2024 SPM calculation used one sex category split equally into females and males, fixed biological schedules and selectivity, and stochastic recruitment generated from the historical arithmetic and harmonic means with an inverse-Gaussian distribution. Its 1,000 simulations retained recruitment process variability; uncertainty in fitted abundance, mean recruitment, selectivity and weights was omitted. The saved seed is 123 in the historical SPM source.</p>
<p>The recovered 2024 handoff uses five preceding selectivity years (2019–2023), April spawning, the terminal spawning weights and fitted future fishery weights. SPM averages age-one recruitment over 1978–2023; the assessment’s <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>100</mn><mi>%</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{100\%}</annotation></semantics></math> calculation includes 2024. These different recruitment means produce different reference-point values. The selected scenario fixes catches at 1,350 kt in both 2025 and 2026. Its archived simulation means provide the historical forecast comparison.</p>
</section>
</section>
<section class="level2 unnumbered safe-appendix-heading" id="sec-ftnir-appendix">
<h2 class="unnumbered safe-appendix-heading anchored" data-anchor-id="sec-ftnir-appendix"><span class="safe-appendix-label"><strong>Appendix G</strong></span><br/>
<span class="safe-appendix-title"><strong>FT-NIRS Age Prediction for EBS Pollock</strong></span></h2>
<!-- Generated by scripts/sync_ftnir_appendix.py from the canonical wiki. Edit the wiki body/supplements, then rebuild; do not edit this snapshot. -->
<p>Authored by: Derek Chamberlin, Esther Goldstein, Beth Matta, and Jason Conner</p>
<p>FT-NIRS Team: John Brogan, Jason Conner, Derek Chamberlin, Esther Goldstein, Brenna Hsieh, Beth Matta, Jon Short</p>
<p>FT-NIRS predicts age from otolith spectra and associated specimen information, using traditional microscopic ages for calibration and validation. The workflow proceeds from age prediction through tester-age conversion to the assessment likelihood (<a class="quarto-xref" href="#tbl-ftnir-treatment">Table G1</a>). The 2024 and 2025 fishery age compositions use their respective independent tester-age keys applied to released FT-NIRS predictions. The 2025 source is model a00-d3. The year-specific keys also convert biological weight inputs (<a class="quarto-xref" href="#tbl-ftnir-conversion-status">Table G2</a>). Both composition series use the assessment’s identity ageing-error assumption after their selected age treatment.</p>
<p>Year-specific conditional keys redistribute source abundance and biomass among tester ages. Mean weights are then calculated as converted biomass divided by converted abundance, with terminal ages pooled using those totals. The partial 2024 fishery diagnostic retains unsupported source-age-13 mass (<a class="quarto-xref" href="#tbl-ftnir-fishery-2024-weights">Table G3</a>). Selected assessment weights fill that row using pooled age offsets and assign a 100% CV to the target-age-15+ weight observation. The 2025 conversion uses 668 independent tester pairs and fills the unsupported source-age-13 row with the midpoint of the age-12 and age-14 conditional probabilities. The same key supplies the 2025 age composition and weight observations (<a class="quarto-xref" href="#tbl-ftnir-fishery-weights">Table G4</a>).</p>
<p>BTS 2025 and 2026 use separate tester-age keys. The 2026 key retains 307 pairs after excluding 22 flagged pairs, with exact TMA ages 1–18 converted before ages 15–18 are pooled into 15+. Total abundance and biomass are conserved. Converted weight SEs propagate the saved joint abundance–weight covariance (<a class="quarto-xref" href="#tbl-ftnir-bts-weights">Table G5</a>). The fitted weight model retains its existing marginal observation likelihood, and empirical-key uncertainty is excluded. Numerical checks distinguish fitted use from the retained full-pair conversion diagnostics (<a class="quarto-xref" href="#tbl-ftnir-checks">Table G6</a>).</p>
<p>Provisional 2026 ATS ages use the BTS age–length key (ALK) applied to ATS population length-frequency estimates, followed by conversion to the TMA basis. FT-NIRS ages from the 2026 ATS samples will be available in 2027. Unsupported lengths remain unallocated. The resulting weights also supply the 2026 AVO predictions.</p>
<!-- Generated by scripts/sync_ftnir_appendix.py from the canonical wiki. Edit the wiki body/supplements, then rebuild; do not edit this snapshot. -->
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="sec-ftnir-overview">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="sec-ftnir-overview">Fourier transform near-infrared spectroscopy (FT-NIRS) Overview</h3>
<p>Fourier transform near-infrared spectroscopy (FT-NIRS) has emerged as an effective secondary age prediction tool and has successfully been implemented in production ageing settings (Matta and Helser, 2024), with FT-NIRS predicted ages recently being used to produce stock assessment age composition data (Dick et al., 2025; Ianelli, 2025). FT-NIRS is a non-destructive technique that interrogates a sample using light in the near-infrared region of the light spectrum (typically 4,000 to 12,000 cm<sup>-1</sup>).</p>
<p>Scanning with FT-NIRS produces a spectral signature of the sample based on the absorption of near infrared light by different chemical bonds, such as C-H (aliphatic), C-H (aromatic), C-O (carboxyl), O-H (hydroxyl), and N-H (amine and amide) (Murray and Williams, 1987). For otoliths, these spectra capture changes in the organic protein matrix (otolin) relative to the inorganic calcium carbonate structure. This relationship correlates strongly with fish growth and age (Passerotti et al., 2022) and has been used to develop models, calibrated with traditional microscopic ages (TMA) and FT-NIR spectra, to predict the age of unknown samples based on their spectral signatures with an estimated time-cost saving of 23-40% (Adamack et al., 2025). FT-NIRS has been applied to estimate age for a multitude of fish species from Australia (Wedding et al., 2014), the Mediterranean Sea (Basilone et al., 2024), the eastern Bering Sea (Benson et al., 2023), and the Atlantic Ocean (Adamack et al., 2025).</p>
</section>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="sec-ftnir-tma-qaqc">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="sec-ftnir-tma-qaqc">Traditional Microscopic Ageing (TMA) QA/QC</h3>
<p>The FT-NIRS models rely on traditional microscopic ageing (TMA) to calibrate the model, thus the accuracy of the age predictions is directly impacted by the accuracy of the calibration ages (Chamberlin et al., 2026). The AFSC Age and Growth Program (AGP) has a long history of ageing walleye pollock by microscopic examination of otolith growth patterns (Matta et al., 2026) and has employed a rigorous quality control program since 1983 (Kimura and Anderl, 2005). In TMA of pollock, presumed annual marks (“annuli”) are enumerated from the otolith surface in younger fish or from burned or toasted otolith cross sections in older fish (Matta and Kimura, 2012; Matta et al., 2026). The accuracy of the AGP’s TMA for pollock has been independently corroborated using a variety of methods, including radiometric ageing, edge and marginal increment analysis, year-class tracking, and captive-rearing studies (Kastelle and Kimura, 2006; Kimura et al., 2006; Kimura et al., 2007; Lai, 1985).</p>
<p>To test FT-NIRS model prediction skill, random 20% subsamples of pollock otoliths from each collection source (fishery, bottom-trawl survey, and hydroacoustic midwater trawl) were subjected to TMA. Spectral outliers (i.e., those that predicted fish lengths outside an established threshold) were also selected for TMA; see <a href="#sec-ftnir-qaqc">FT-NIRS QA/QC below</a> for more details. Each otolith selected for TMA was independently aged by two experienced readers. The TMA subsamples were evaluated for inter-reader precision and bias. All discrepancies between the two readers were resolved. Any TMA age-length outliers were reexamined, and re-aged or classified as collection errors when appropriate (Kimura and Anderl, 2005).</p>
</section>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="sec-ftnir-qaqc">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="sec-ftnir-qaqc">FT-NIRS QA/QC</h3>
<p>In addition to the TMA QA/QC, the FT-NIR spectra underwent a three-step QA/QC process to identify poor quality spectra due to data collection errors, instrument issues, or otolith irregularities such as crystallization, contamination, or fragmentation (Goldstein et al., 2024). Spectrometer operators conducted qualitative QA/QC concurrent with data collection to identify missing data and unusual spectra using length predictions from a species- and region-specific partial least-squares regression (PLSR) model in comparison to observed lengths. Real-time length predictions were used to identify transcription errors and provide assurance of proper instrument function.</p>
<p>Following data collection, rigorous QA/QC was conducted to identify outliers using principal component analysis (PCA) and PLSR models developed from a multi-year collection of spectral data from each data source (AFSC groundfish survey, AFSC hydroacoustic survey, fishery data) and projections (PCA) and predictions (PLSR) of new data. PCA scores by scan date were used to visually identify instrument drift. Gross spectral data outliers were identified from PCA using Hotelling’s T<sup>2</sup> and Q residuals (Pomerantsev and Rodionova, 2014) and PLSR outlier analyses identified discrepancies between spectra and specimen length by combining Hotelling’s T<sup>2</sup> and Q residuals (full X-distance) and Y-distance (observed vs. predicted; Rodionova and Pomerantsev, 2020). Analyses used a threshold of 1% to identify outliers. Outliers were then aged using traditional microscopic methods. Once aged, outlier spectra were excluded from the final dataset if age predictions from the MMCNN models were also outside the MMCNN 95% Monte Carlo dropout prediction intervals <a href="#sec-ftnir-model">discussed below</a>.</p>
</section>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="sec-ftnir-model">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="sec-ftnir-model">FT-NIRS Model</h3>
<p>Age was predicted from FT-NIR spectra using a multimodal convolutional neural network model (MMCNN). MMCNNs identify non-linear relationships in spectral data, incorporate additional inputs such as fish length or capture location, and learn relevant spectral features during training. Classical chemometric approaches such as PLS require the user to select key wavenumbers (Chen and Wang, 2019). The MMCNN used here is an updated version of the MMCNN presented in Benson et al. (2023) and Chamberlin et al. (2026). The MMCNN includes one convolutional layer and six dense layers to predict age from spectral and fish-length data.</p>
<p>The first layer of the MMCNN is the spectral input data which is fed to a 1D convolutional layer, which acts as an automated feature extractor to identify patterns in the spectra. This output is then processed with a Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) activation function to introduce nonlinearity into the network necessary for approximating continuous functions (Brownlee, 2019; Géron, 2019). The data are then flattened into a one-dimensional array and passed through a dense layer (all dense layers use Exponential Linear Unit (ELU) activation). This reduces the dimensionality of the spectral input and balances its contribution relative to the metadata. The metadata input is fed to a dense layer, then concatenated with the spectral input layer. The output is passed through a fully connected dense layer with ELU activation to model the interactions between spectral data and metadata. To mitigate overfitting, 5 dropout layers follow each dense layer to randomly ignore a subset of neurons and prevent codependency between nodes (Srivastava et al., 2014). Crucially, these dropout layers remain active during the inference phase, a technique known as Monte Carlo (MC) dropout, allowing the model to perform multiple forward passes per sample to generate a distribution of age estimates and calculate Monte Carlo prediction intervals. Finally, a fully connected dense layer with a single node and a batch normalization layer are used to produce a continuous age estimate, allowing for loss estimation via a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) function. The model’s hyperparameters (the number of filters in the convolutional layer, the number of nodes in the concatenated layer, learning rate, batch size and the dropout rate) were optimized using hyperband optimization (Li et al., 2018) with early stopping.</p>
<p>The walleye pollock model is trained on spectra and TMA ages from 2014-2025 using an “n−1” annual model updating approach. Under this scheme, spectral and age data from all fleets up to the year prior to the target prediction year are included (for example, predicting 2025 fishery ages uses data from 2024 and earlier). For MMCNN training, input data are first split into development (80%) and testing (20%) pools using a randomly shuffled split that is stratified on fleet and year. Samples receive a normalized weighting score based on 2 coefficients: <em>decay</em> is an integer [1, 2, 3] that defines the rate of exponential decay for samples based on year, and <em>alpha</em> [0, 0.1, 0.2, …, 1.0] defines whether sample year or sample age frequency has more influence in weighting the sample, with <em>alpha</em> = 1 turning decay off. This allows for testing of whether model performance improves when more recent calibration data or rare age classes are weighted more heavily. For hyperparameter optimization, the development data are further split into training (90%) and validation (10%) datasets to inform early stopping, using the previously defined sample weights. For each scenario a series of 10 trainings, with random seeds, are run to estimate the median number of epochs needed to train the model but avoid overfitting, prior to a final training run based on the median number of epochs.</p>
<p>In total, 31 training models were produced with a grid search for the 2 sample weighting coefficients, and age predictions were generated for bottom trawl survey, hydroacoustic survey and fishery fleets. The final candidate model for each fleet was selected using four statistical metrics: Lin’s concordance correlation coefficient (Lin’s CCC), the mean Winkler score, R<sup>2</sup>, and the slope of the regression between FT-NIRS predicted ages and corresponding TMA ages. Lin’s CCC measures how closely the observed data aligns with a 45° line of perfect agreement, while the mean Winkler score evaluates average performance based on the width of the Monte Carlo prediction intervals and the frequency of samples falling outside them. The four metrics capture different aspects of model accuracy, and visual assessments complemented them. Ultimately, the best-performing model was identified by synthesizing these visual and quantitative criteria. Age predictions were then finalized by removing any samples that were both flagged as a spectral outlier and an outlier from the Monte Carlo prediction intervals. This finalized dataset was then transmitted to end users and coded as FT-NIRS predicted ages.</p>
</section>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="sec-ftnir-treatment">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="sec-ftnir-treatment">Age conversion and assessment use</h3>
<p>The assessment uses year-specific independent tester TMA conversions for the 2024 and 2025 fishery compositions, matching annual weight conversions and separate survey-specific age conversions (<a class="quarto-xref" href="#tbl-ftnir-treatment">Table G1</a>). These treatments serve different purposes: predicting age from spectra, allocating abundance and biomass among ages, and specifying the assessment likelihood are separate steps. Current input and fit records establish their use; the retained partial-conversion diagnostics describe their original support and uncertainty limits.</p>
<p>The 2026 BTS conditional tester-age key excludes calibration pairs marked <code>nir_outlier = Y</code>, removing 22 of 329 complete pairs and retaining 307. It targets independent <code>test_age</code> conditional on FT-NIRS <code>final_nir_age</code>; each FT-NIRS row is normalized by its retained paired count. Conversion uses exact TMA ages 1–18 before pooling ages 15–18 into 15+. Screening applies to calibration pairs, preserving the released abundance vector. All unflagged complete pairs are eligible, including checks outside the systematic 20% sample.</p>
<p>Screening changed the exact mean converted age from 5.318978 to 5.316448 years, with a largest age-proportion change of approximately 0.124 percentage points and unchanged total abundance. The same 307-pair key supplies BTS weight means and their joint-covariance delta-method SEs, provisional ATS age allocations and biomass-derived weights, and the 2026 AVO prediction weights. The standalone RE-WAA refit and assessment fits using these inputs are complete <a href="#ftnir-source-s10">S10</a>. The 2025 BTS key is unchanged. The original 329-pair products remain historical evidence. Empirical-key uncertainty is excluded; the fitted weight model retains its existing marginal observation likelihood rather than using the full converted covariance as a new likelihood.</p>
<p>The contribution describes <strong>31 MMCNN training candidates</strong>, distinguished by sample-weight settings and fleet-specific selection. PCA and PLSR provide spectral QA/QC; PLSR also provides length predictions. The <code>a00-d3</code> and <code>a03-d1</code> labels on the <a href="https://bookish-chainsaw-o8jopw4.pages.github.io/ftnir-prediction-overlay.html">saved 600-fish comparison</a> identify prediction sets, separately from the assessment’s cumulative <code>0.x</code> input sequence.</p>
