<section class="level4 unnumbered" id="sec-ftnir-model-levels">
<h4 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="sec-ftnir-model-levels">Predictive model and assessment input differences</h4>
<p>The MMCNN combines spectral and fish-length information, MC dropout prediction intervals, hyperband optimization and 31 sample-weight settings. Its annual n−1 updating rule uses information available before the prediction year; for example, a 2025 prediction uses data through 2024. The selected fleet-by-year model checksum, coefficient setting and exact mapping to the saved 600-fish prediction files remain to be documented.</p>
<p>The full tester-key release uses <code>final_nir_age</code> as predictor and independent <code>test_age</code> as target, excluding resolved <code>final_age</code> as the calibration target. It contains 3,000 fishery-2025 records, 1,638 BTS-2025 records and 1,586 BTS-2026 records; 2,992, 1,619 and 1,582 have released FT-NIRS ages. Their complete-pair counts are 668, 390 and 329, respectively; the screened 2026 BTS application retains 307 <a href="#ftnir-source-s1">S1</a>.</p>
<p>For the 2025 fishery, model a00-d3 FT-NIRS ages are converted to independent tester ages using the 668 complete paired observations. The conditional probability of tester age <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> given FT-NIRS age <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> is <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mi>/</mi><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>j</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{ij}=n_{ij}/\sum_j n_{ij}</annotation></semantics></math>. Converted numbers are <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mi>j</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow></msubsup><msub><mi>K</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N^{\mathrm{TMA}}_j=\sum_i N^{\mathrm{FTNIR}}_iK_{ij}</annotation></semantics></math>. Empirical rows retain the released paired observations, including flagged pairs. The unsupported source-age-13 row is <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mrow><mn>13</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mrow><mn>14</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{13,j}=(K_{12,j}+K_{14,j})/2</annotation></semantics></math>, giving probabilities of one third at tester age 10, one sixth at age 11 and one half at age 15. The age-12 row has six pairs and the age-14 row one pair, so this interpolation has limited direct support. Source and tester ages in the release are exact ages 2–15; the assessment terminal group contains ages 15 and older. The selected likelihood sample size is 530. The key is treated as fixed; empirical-key and interpolation uncertainty are excluded.</p>
<p>The 2024 fishery composition uses its 693-pair independent tester key. The unsupported source-age-13 row uses pooled TMA-minus-FT-NIRS offsets from the same year’s source ages 9–12 (34 pairs). Empirical rows remain unchanged; the selected likelihood input is 578. Both recent years are converted before fitting and use a 15-by-15 identity ageing-error matrix, equivalent to the ADMB setting with ageing error switched off. Key and tail-allocation uncertainty are additional to the sampling precision represented by the selected likelihood weights.</p>
<p>Weight conversion applies the same conditional key to source numbers and biomass, then divides converted biomass by converted numbers. Terminal-age weights use pooled totals. The partial empirical 2024 diagnostic leaves unsupported source-age-13 mass unallocated. The selected weight treatment fills that row using pooled offsets from source ages 9–12 and assigns a 100% CV to the target-age-15+ observation. Those fixed approximations add no empirical calibration pairs; their uncertainty differs from a sampling SE. The 2025 weight observations use the same source-age-13 midpoint as the age composition. Their zero-abundance source-age-1 padding contributes no converted numbers or biomass. The midpoint is specific to 2025; source age 14 also lacks pairs in the 2024 key.</p>
<p>The older staging record <a href="#ftnir-source-s6">S6</a> describes a 2024 endpoint in <code>pm_26_candidate.dat</code>: fishery CAA at 0.4, provisional BTS WAA/biomass at 0.5/0.6, ATS at 0.7, and separate AVO-only 0.8/0.9 components. These are historical input-sequence labels from the <a href="https://bookish-chainsaw-o8jopw4.pages.github.io/incremental-models-2026.html">incremental-model plan</a>. Current fitted use follows the documented working input and run records, not those earlier staging exclusions.</p>
</section>
<section class="level4 unnumbered" id="sec-ftnir-treatment-pending">
<h4 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="sec-ftnir-treatment-pending">Source and validation limits</h4>
<p>The partial 2024 empirical diagnostic retains its unsupported source-age-13 mass. Selected assessment weights use the pooled-offset rule and 100% CV described above. The 2024 and 2025 compositions use their respective tester-age keys and selected support rules. Weight SEs propagate the available joint abundance–weight covariance, while the fitted model retains its marginal observation likelihood. Empirical-key uncertainty remains excluded.</p>
<p>The assessment author identified a00-d3 as the selected 2025 fishery model. The exact training-run checksum, coefficient setting and complete collection-by-year release record remain to be documented. The 31 predictive candidates and the assessment’s cumulative input stages identify different choices. The earlier mixed-basis BTS workbook remains unavailable; the separately identified current workbook is excluded from assessment assembly. Its source basis must be established before using it in a comparison.</p>
<p>Provisional ATS products retain their transferred BTS age–length and tester-age keys, unsupported-length limits and separate sampling conditions. Direct ATS age and weight validation remains open, with age-composition data expected in 2027. Archived full-pair calibration products remain available alongside the screened-key input records. Prior fit, projection and posterior records retain their original dates and input identities. Final model and recommendation selection remain separate review decisions.</p>
</section>
<section class="level4 unnumbered" id="sec-ftnir-treatment-sources">
<h4 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="sec-ftnir-treatment-sources">Sources and reproducibility</h4>
<p>The paired-age releases, preparation products and current run records retain their source identities. Detailed file locations, checksums and the original preparation narrative are preserved in the technical source record.</p>
<ul>
<li><span id="ftnir-source-s1"><strong>S1 — Paired tester-age release</strong></span>: the full year-specific tester-key workbook and tidy release, with independent tester ages as the calibration target.</li>
<li><span id="ftnir-source-s2"><strong>S2 — Fishery observations</strong></span>: catch-expanded annual numbers based on released FT-NIRS ages, with year-specific tester-age conversions: 693 pairs and N=578 for 2024; 668 pairs and N=530 for 2025.</li>
<li><span id="ftnir-source-s3"><strong>S3 — Weight conversion</strong></span>: year-specific fishery conversion keys, partial 2024 diagnostics and independent fishery arithmetic checks.</li>
<li><span id="ftnir-source-s4"><strong>S4 — Survey age compositions</strong></span>: revised BTS abundance and proportion estimates, with their source age assignments.</li>
<li><span id="ftnir-source-s5"><strong>S5 — Survey weights and covariance</strong></span>: matching model-based abundance and weight estimates, joint covariance and delta-method validation.</li>
<li><span id="ftnir-source-s6"><strong>S6 — Historical staging</strong></span>: the earlier preparation sequence, retained separately from current selected input and fit records.</li>
<li><span id="ftnir-source-s7"><strong>S7 — Earlier age comparison</strong></span>: fishery and survey comparisons for 2014–2018, distinct from later training and prediction releases.</li>
<li><span id="ftnir-source-s8"><strong>S8 — ATS length-to-age calculation</strong></span>: the 2024 age–length workbook and expanded number/biomass calculations.</li>
<li><span id="ftnir-source-s9"><strong>S9 — ATS survey products</strong></span>: regional survey length and biomass products used for the provisional BTS-key transfer.</li>
<li><span id="ftnir-source-s10"><strong>S10 — Current screened-key inputs and fits</strong></span>: the 307-pair calibration, completed standalone RE-WAA refit and current assessment run records. The original 329-pair products retain their historical identity.</li>
</ul>
</section>
</section>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="sec-ftnir-weight-patterns">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="sec-ftnir-weight-patterns">Year-specific weight-conversion diagnostics</h3>
<p>The retained full-pair conversion record separates three completed year-specific conversions from the partial 2024 fishery diagnostic (<a href="#adj-tbl-conversion-status">conversion-status table</a>). Fishery 2025 and BTS 2025–2026 use independent tester-age keys; positive unsupported source-age-13 mass remains unallocated in fishery 2024.</p>
<p>Mean weights generally increase with age, with the largest source-versus- converted differences concentrated at older ages (<a href="#adj-tbl-fishery-2024-weights">2024 fishery weight table</a>). The partial fishery 2024 values at TMA ages 13 and 14 are both 1.2878 kg, while its target 15+ weight remains missing. Its prepared older-age SEs are large relative to the means; the partial converted SDs condition on the fixed key and supported source ages.</p>
<p>The 2025 fishery conversion raises the 15+ mean from 0.8102 to 1.2676 kg; target ages 13 and 14 retain missing weights because converted abundance is zero (<a href="#adj-tbl-fishery-weights">fishery weight comparison</a>). Thus the older-age differences include changes in support as well as in ratios.</p>
<p>BTS 2025 converted weights are generally below the source weights from age 5 upward; in 2026, weights at ages 3–8 remain close to or above their source values, while older-age weights are lower (<a href="#adj-tbl-bts-weights">BTS weight comparison</a>; <a class="quarto-xref" href="#fig-ftnir-assessment-weights">Figure G1</a>). The 15+ mean changes from 1.7646 to 1.5474 kg in 2025 and from 1.8390 to 1.3665 kg in 2026. These are conversion contrasts that vary by age and year. The smaller conditional SEs in several converted cells retain the stated fixed-key uncertainty scope.</p>
<p>Independent fishery arithmetic, preservation of earlier fishery values and survey covariance/derivative checks establish computational consistency (<a href="#adj-tbl-checks">conversion checks</a>). The partial 2024 diagnostic leaves unsupported source-age-13 mass unallocated. Current selected weights use the separate pooled-offset tail treatment and 100% CV, and the screened-key standalone RE-WAA and assessment fits are complete. These distinctions preserve the historical diagnostic’s support limits and the current fit’s fixed-key uncertainty scope.</p>

<section class="level4 unnumbered" id="adj-current-status">
<h4 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="adj-current-status">Diagnostic basis and current use</h4>
<p>The retained diagnostics convert fishery <strong>2025</strong> and BTS <strong>2025–2026</strong> abundance and biomass with their year-specific independent tester-age keys. Fishery <strong>2024</strong> has a distinct 693-pair key, but its empirical partial conversion leaves positive source-age-13 mass unallocated. The selected assessment weight treatment fills that row using pooled offsets from source ages 9–12 and assigns a 100% CV to the target-age-15+ weight observation. The current standalone RE-WAA refit and assessment fits are complete; the historical partial diagnostic remains separate. The BTS tables below retain the original full-pair calibration, while the current 2026 fit uses the screened 307-pair key.</p>

<section class="level4 unnumbered" id="adj-conversion-and-approved-approximations">
<h4 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="adj-conversion-and-approved-approximations">Conversion and approved approximations</h4>
<p>Each key gives the distribution of TMA tester age conditional on FTNIR age. Abundance and biomass are redistributed together, using the same conditional probabilities. Converted mean weight is converted biomass divided by converted abundance. Within a source FTNIR bin, this calculation assigns the same source mean weight to every target age.</p>
<p>For fishery 2025, Jim approved two rules for unsupported source ages:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Age 1:</strong> a dummy identity row assigns FTNIR age 1 to TMA age 1. All saved source age-1 catch estimates are zero, so this row retains zero catch.</li>
<li><strong>Age 13:</strong> each target-age probability is the arithmetic average of its probabilities in the source age-12 and age-14 rows. The resulting row sums to one. This approximation uses the existing age-12 and age-14 pairs.</li>
</ul>
<p>Converted target-age 13 and 14 abundances are zero in the 2025 fishery key. Their weights and SEs remain paired missing observations. The historical data continue to inform these ages in the future wtAgeRE fit. All pre-2025 fishery mean/SE decimal values are preserved exactly.</p>
<p>Exact BTS target ages 1–18 are retained during conversion. Target ages 15–18 are then pooled into 15+, conserving total abundance and biomass. The 2024 fishery key also retains exact target ages through 18; the 2025 fishery key has target ages through 15. The same terminal pooling convention applies. Age selection for wtAgeRE occurs after conversion; its input bins are 3–15+.</p>
</section>
<section class="level4 unnumbered" id="adj-fishery-2024-results-and-remaining-gap">
<h4 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="adj-fishery-2024-results-and-remaining-gap">Fishery 2024 results and remaining gap</h4>
<p>The recovered 2024 release contains <strong>2,985 released FTNIR ages and 693 complete independent tester pairs</strong>. The target is <code>test_age</code>; the resolved <code>final_age</code> is a separate field. Canonical specimen and age-field hashes match the independent original-workbook verification record. The original workbook itself remains outside this local snapshot. The empirical key uses all complete released pairs, including additional QA/QC selections; their representativeness remains an assumption.</p>
<p>Source ages <strong>1–12</strong> have empirical probability rows. Source ages <strong>13–15</strong> lack pairs; only age 13 has positive mass in the saved sampler draws. Its unallocated observed-point mass is <strong>0.0323% of abundance</strong> and <strong>0.0817% of biomass</strong>. Allocated plus unallocated totals balance across all 1,001 saved rows to relative errors below 6.7e-16. The diagnostic retains that mass separately and preserves the original totals.</p>
<p>The table and figure report the <strong>partial, fixed-key bootstrap mean and SD</strong> from the supported source rows. Every converted 2024 bin remains conditional on the unresolved source-age-13 allocation. Target TMA age 15+ receives zero allocated abundance, so its mean and SD remain missing. Source FTNIR age 13 and target TMA age 13 are distinct: supported source ages can populate target ages 13 and 14.</p>
<p>The 2025 midpoint rule stays specific to its approved key. In 2024, source age 14 also lacks calibration pairs; applying the age-12/14 midpoint rule would require additional empirical support. The 2024 key supports source age 1 directly; its positive source catch is retained.</p>

<p>Converted fishery weights and bootstrap SDs are recalculated from the first 1,000 paired sampler bootstrap draws after transforming each draw’s abundance and biomass. The final observed-data point row is excluded from those summaries. The previously selected legacy convention is retained: a target age absent in a bootstrap draw has zero weight for that draw. The SD uses the sample denominator. Known limitations of the legacy sampler’s resampling selectors remain in the source record.</p>
<p>BTS uncertainty uses the saved joint VAST parameter covariance and conditional random-effect covariance. It includes dependence between source abundance and weight, among ages through shared parameters, and between 2025 and 2026. The ratio’s numerator and denominator both contribute to the delta-method SE. The calculation evaluates the saved VAST model at its parameter estimates.</p>
<p><strong>All conversion keys are treated as fixed.</strong> The reported SEs exclude uncertainty in the empirical keys, the dummy row, and the interpolated row.</p>

<p>The source records retain matching abundance and weight estimates from the same saved survey fit, along with input/output hashes and fixed-key approximation rules. The empirical key is treated as fixed. Current fitting records and the historical conversion diagnostics are identified separately in the technical source record.</p>
<p>The historical 2024 partial-conversion diagnostics preserve their original inputs and supported-age limits. The current selected tail allocation, screened BTS key and completed fits have separate source and run identities. Earlier preparation states and the original verification wording remain archived in the technical source record.</p>
<p>This is an internal methods record. It uses a compact Quarto report and TAF-compatible source, transformation, output, and provenance stages. Assessment adoption is documented in the separate input and run records.</p>
<ul>
<li>Historical partial-diagnostic fishery input: converted 2025, preserved 2024</li>
<li>Converted BTS input</li>
<li>Fishery approximation key</li>
<li>Conversion manifest</li>
<li>BTS uncertainty validation</li>
<li>2024 empirical key</li>
<li>2024 partial bootstrap summaries</li>
<li>2024 exact and pooled point candidates</li>
<li>2024 key support and unallocated source mass</li>
<li>2024 validation</li>
</ul>
<p>Complete numbered conversion report · Editable analytical Quarto source · Subsection source manifest</p>

<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="sec-ftnir-ats-age-compositions">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="sec-ftnir-ats-age-compositions">Provisional ATS age compositions</h3>
<p>In 2026, ATS age compositions were estimated by borrowing the BTS age–length keys and applying them to ATS abundance-at-length data. Following usual practice, age data for the 2026 ATS length samples will be applied in 2027.</p>
</section>

<section class="level2 unnumbered safe-appendix-heading" id="sec-bts-spatiotemporal-appendix">
<h2 class="unnumbered safe-appendix-heading anchored" data-anchor-id="sec-bts-spatiotemporal-appendix"><span class="safe-appendix-label"><strong>Appendix H</strong></span><br/>
<span class="safe-appendix-title"><strong>BTS Spatiotemporal Biomass Index and Abundance at Age, Including the Northern Bering Sea</strong></span></h2>
<p>This appendix describes the spatiotemporal modeling approach used to estimate the bottom-trawl survey (BTS) biomass index and abundance at age for the combined eastern and northern Bering Sea (EBS and NBS). This approach was adopted in the 2024 assessment for both abundance at age and survey indices and follows the approach used by the AFSC Groundfish Assessment Program (GAP) in previous assessments. The sections below describe its application to the 2026 survey data, including model specifications and uncertainty estimates.</p>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="scope-and-relationship-to-the-earlier-vast-appendix">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="scope-and-relationship-to-the-earlier-vast-appendix">Scope and relationship to the earlier VAST appendix</h3>
<p>The earlier VAST appendix describes a different software generation and mixed 1982–2023/2024 coverage. It is retained as a historical source. The description uses the settings in the saved production fit objects. The saved production fit objects identify <strong>sdmTMB 1.0.0</strong> for the biomass index and <strong>tinyVAST 1.6.3</strong> for abundance at age. Model-based integration across EBS and NBS extends the approach used to address pollock distribution shifts <span class="citation" data-cites="OLeary2020">(<a href="#ref-OLeary2020" role="doc-biblioref">O’Leary et al. 2020</a>)</span>. The sdmTMB framework is described by <span class="citation" data-cites="Anderson2022">Anderson et al. (<a href="#ref-Anderson2022" role="doc-biblioref">2022</a>)</span>.</p>
<p>Both output series contain <strong>44 years, 1982–2019 and 2021–2026</strong>. The survey was absent in 2020. The index fit retains 2020 as an additional latent time step representing a model prediction. The age fit retains annual time levels across 1982–2026, while the abundance and composition data files omit 2020. NBS sampling coverage varies among years within the prediction domain.</p>
</section>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="biomass-index">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="biomass-index">Biomass index</h3>
<p>The pollock index code reads density-dependence-corrected station biomass density from the VAST-named input file. The file name is historical; the saved model class is sdmTMB. Input density is converted from kg/ha to kg/km² by multiplying by 100. The saved fit uses a Poisson-link delta-gamma observation model with separate year effects and spatial and spatiotemporal fields. Both components have spatial fields and annual AR(1) spatiotemporal structure. The retained call enables geometric anisotropy and includes a spatially varying coefficient for the environmental covariate.</p>
<p>The companion pollock code defines that covariate as standardized cold-pool area, the area of bottom water at or below 2°C <span class="citation" data-cites="rohan2022">(<a href="#ref-rohan2022" role="doc-biblioref">Rohan et al. 2022</a>)</span>. The saved object contains its numerical covariate and the formula; the complete annual cold-pool release manifest remains unavailable. The exact environmental release and production script revision require confirmation.</p>
<p>Predicted density is integrated over a fixed regional grid. For grid-cell area (A_{r,j}) in km² and predicted biomass density (d_{t,j}) in kg/km², the regional biomass index in tons is</p>
<p><span id="eq-bts-spatial-biomass"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover><mi>I</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>1000</mn></mfrac><munder><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></munder><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mover><mi>d</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mi>.</mi><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\widehat I_{r,t}=\frac{1}{1000}\sum_{j\in r}A_{r,j}\widehat d_{t,j}.
 \qquad(20)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>The biomass-index estimates include separate EBS, NBS and combined <strong>Both</strong> products. The combined 2026 point estimate is <strong>9,034,017.809 t</strong>; the separate EBS and NBS point estimates sum to that value within numerical precision. These survey estimates remain subject to assessment input selection and acceptance.</p>
</section>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="abundance-at-age">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="abundance-at-age">Abundance at age</h3>
<p>The saved tinyVAST fit uses numerical density at station and age, with age-by-year fixed effects in both delta components. All 15 labelled age classes have age-specific spatial variance terms and a common estimated lag-1 temporal coefficient in the spatiotemporal specification. The saved control has anisotropy disabled. This model uses age-by-year effects with the environmental terms excluded.</p>
<p>The companion pollock code multiplies CPUE_num by 100, converting fish/ha to fish/km². Its comment describing this as a conversion of kg is inconsistent with the numerical input; the calculation is an abundance calculation. Numerical density is integrated over the combined EBS–NBS grid and scaled to billions of fish:</p>
<p><span id="eq-bts-spatial-abundance"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover><mi>N</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mspace width="0.278em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mspace width="0.222em"></mspace><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi></mrow><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">]</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>9</mn></msup></mfrac><munder><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></munder><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mover><mi>n</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msub><mover><mi>p</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mover><mi>N</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>b</mi></munder><msub><mover><mi>N</mi><mo accent="true">̂</mo></mover><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mi>.</mi><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>21</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\widehat N_{r,t,a}\;[\mathrm{billion\ fish}]
=\frac{1}{10^9}\sum_{j\in r}A_{r,j}\widehat n_{t,a,j},
\qquad
\widehat p_{r,t,a}=
\frac{\widehat N_{r,t,a}}{\sum_b\widehat N_{r,t,b}}.
 \qquad(21)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
<p>The abundance-at-age matrix contains 15 rows and 44 year columns. Its row order agrees with the companion age_1 through age_15 composition columns: normalizing every matrix column reproduces the composition file to a maximum absolute difference of (8.4^{-16}). The 2026 combined total is <strong>16.064690 billion fish</strong>. The companion composition file supplies the age labels for the matrix and must remain attached to it. Displayed ages are 1–14 and 15+; the terminal category represents fish aged 15 and older. The original source column names are retained in the data. The age export supplies only the combined EBS–NBS estimates (terminal-age interpretation).</p>
<p>These expanded compositions use the age assignments and age–length-key preparation in their station-level inputs. Age assignment and FT-NIRS-to-traditional-age conversion precede the tinyVAST expansion. The exact release, assignment rules for 2025–2026, and any age-age correction used in this production input remain part of the source reconciliation.</p>
</section>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="verified-settings-and-prediction-code-evidence">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="verified-settings-and-prediction-code-evidence">Verified settings and prediction-code evidence</h3>
<p>The retained index fit uses 250 interior mesh knots, anisotropy and a spatially varying environmental coefficient; the age fit uses 50 interior knots with anisotropy disabled and a separate spatial variance structure by age (<a class="quarto-xref" href="#tbl-bts-spatial-settings">Table H1</a>). Prediction-grid and integration settings are identified separately as companion-code evidence. The local code checkout is 2a9e6f26062d34ee0375f8eac9462e51273e65a3. Its default species selections are Pacific cod for the index and yellowfin sole for age compositions. The saved pollock fit objects supply the production evidence for this appendix; the generic default selections remain code context.</p>

<p>The code grid has 492,989.921 km² in the EBS and 198,866.805 km² in the NBS, summing to 691,856.726 km². Those grid files are hashed in the source record. The complete production prediction grid and expansion invocation remain unavailable. This draft therefore distinguishes companion-code settings from verified saved-fit settings. The historical 2-nmi grid and 750-knot index describe the earlier VAST workflow.</p>
</section>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="uncertainty-diagnostics-and-outstanding-review">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="uncertainty-diagnostics-and-outstanding-review">Uncertainty, diagnostics and outstanding review</h3>
<p>The index code requests bias-corrected integration. It also contains a 500-simulation covariance workflow. The assessment selects its covariance file and uncertainty treatment separately from those integration settings. The age expansion code sets bias.correct=FALSE and getsd=FALSE despite apply.epsilon=TRUE. Its age output therefore excludes epsilon bias correction and a full estimated age-composition covariance. Assessment weighting and the selected design-based covariance remain separate decisions.</p>
<p>The saved index object reports a positive definite Hessian and maximum absolute retained gradient <strong>0.0138148</strong>. The saved age object reports optimizer return code 0, a positive definite Hessian and maximum retained gradient <strong>0.000205084</strong>. These diagnostics require provider review for numerical acceptance. Both gradients exceed the workspace’s (10^{-4}) assessment-model convergence guardrail; their suitability for these survey fits requires provider review. This appendix uses the saved survey fits by the provider.</p>
<p>The saved index data have <strong>17,236 rows</strong>, while the adjacent raw index export has <strong>17,237</strong>; the counts differ in 2026 (350 versus 351). The saved age fit has <strong>265,350 rows</strong>, versus <strong>258,555</strong> in the adjacent age-density export. Historical differences occur in 1982, 1985, 1988, 1991, 1994, 2001, 2005, 2006 and 2018; 2026 has 5,250 fitted rows versus 5,265 exported rows. These differences prevent a claim that the saved objects exactly reproduce the neighboring raw files. Their causes, the intended final input versions and the fit-to-export chain require confirmation from the survey analysts.</p>
<p>Before finalizing this appendix, confirm the production script revision, prediction grid, annual environmental release, full R/TMB/dependency versions, age-assignment lineage, treatment of the input mismatches, and the accepted covariance and diagnostic assessment. The latest linked general writeup and terms-of-reference table remain unavailable through the connected source. Their agreement with this draft requires author review. Historical VAST dependency versions retain their original dates.</p>
</section>
<section class="level3 unnumbered" id="source-and-reproducibility-record">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="source-and-reproducibility-record">Source and reproducibility record</h3>
<p>The local provenance bundle retains saved-object metadata and checks, source file hashes, output consistency checks, and the read-only extraction scripts. It also preserves the original historical VAST text and historical PDF. The original fit objects and station-level inputs remain in their owning data directory. The report consumes saved metadata and aggregate outputs.</p>
<p>Current-method source code: <a href="https://github.com/afsc-gap-products/model-based-indices/blob/2a9e6f26062d34ee0375f8eac9462e51273e65a3/R/bs_indices.Rmd">index workflow</a> and <a href="https://github.com/afsc-gap-products/model-based-indices/blob/2a9e6f26062d34ee0375f8eac9462e51273e65a3/R/bs_age_comps.R">age-composition workflow</a>. Author-documents awaiting access: <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nZhbF4GNNDy0JBcmXs8RcGfREV0AiDN-i06PUSkFcKI/edit">general methods writeup</a> and <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wMw02uGw8bwxfBfXqIMnVMXlOA53XxuJ/edit">terms-of-reference settings</a>.</p>
</section>
</section>
<section class="level2 unnumbered safe-appendix-heading" id="review-and-source-record">
<h2 class="unnumbered safe-appendix-heading anchored" data-anchor-id="review-and-source-record"><span class="safe-appendix-label"><strong>Appendix I</strong></span><br/>
<span class="safe-appendix-title"><strong>Assessment Development and Supporting Record</strong></span></h2>
<p>The September 2026 assessment development document <span class="citation" data-cites="ianelli2026developments">(<a href="#ref-ianelli2026developments" role="doc-biblioref">Ianelli et al. 2026</a>)</span>, published 3 September, presents the starting model comparisons and exploratory appendices using data through 2024. Corrected through-2024 results are archived with that document; the main assessment uses observations through 2026.</p>
<p>The Plan Team excerpt provides the seven recommendation summaries (<a class="quarto-xref" href="#tbl-plan-team">Table A1</a>). Its final report citation and any subsequent SSC direction require verification before release.</p>
<p>The source guidelines are <em>Alaska Groundfish Stock Assessment Guidelines</em>, July 2024, in a file named <em>Stock Assessment Guidelines Tier 3.docx</em>. Their publication procedures inform eventual release preparation. The development copy remains local under the user’s release timing.</p>

<tr class="gt_sourcenotes">
<td class="gt_sourcenote" colspan="5">Assessment conclusions are separate from final NMFS determinations. Updated 2025 catch (1,326,215.61 t) is below its 2,957,000-t OFL. For Model 26.1.2, 2026 spawning biomass (3.065 million t) and Alternative 7 biomass in 2028 (3.179 million t) both exceed B35% (2.177 million t), supporting the two 2026 “No” entries. <a href="#sec-status-determination">Section 9</a> describes the status tests. Each two-year column pair reports overfishing for the earlier catch year and stock status for the later assessment year; cells outside those year-specific determinations are marked n/a. <section class="level3 unnumbered" id="assessment-archive-record">
<h3 class="unnumbered anchored" data-anchor-id="assessment-archive-record">Assessment archive record</h3>
<p>The assessment archive links model source and executable versions, prepared inputs, run controls, saved fits, diagnostics, retrospectives, projections and report products. Source manifests document provenance and access restrictions. Scientific acceptance is documented separately from numerical diagnostics and report preparation.</p>
</section>
